hero.headline: Democrats lead Republicans by 8 points in new congressional poll
hero.teaser: A new survey shows Democrats ahead of Republicans on a generic ballot as midterm elections approach.
hero.body:
Democrats hold an 8-point advantage over Republicans on a generic congressional ballot, according to a poll from Emerson College and The Hill. The survey found 50.7 percent of respondents would back a Democrat if midterm elections were held immediately, compared to 43 percent who would support a Republican. Another 6.3 percent remained undecided.

The polling results provide a snapshot of voter sentiment as both parties prepare for the midterm elections. Generic ballot surveys ask voters which party they would support without naming specific candidates, offering a broad measure of the political environment.

cards.headline: Trump announces tougher economic measures against Iran and countries supporting it
cards.teaser: President Trump said he will impose stricter economic measures on Iran and nations that support the country.
cards.body:
President Trump has pledged to intensify economic measures targeting Iran and nations that support it, demanding that Tehran "put up the white flag of surrender." The announcement follows the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire on Monday with no diplomatic or military resolution in sight.

The escalation has immediate market effects, with oil prices rising above $90 per barrel for the first time since late July. Iran responded by signaling it would adopt a more aggressive stance if negotiations with the US fail to progress.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise Following New Threats Against Iran
cards.teaser: Oil prices jumped after President Trump issued new threats against Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices surged after the expiration of a two-month ceasefire between the US and Iran on Monday, with no diplomatic resolution achieved. Brent crude rose above $90 a barrel for the first time since late July. The escalation reflects renewed tensions following Trump's demand that Iran "surrender," while Iranian officials signaled they would adopt a more aggressive stance if negotiations with the US fail.

The price movement underscores trader concerns about potential disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies. Bond markets also experienced volatility as investors assessed the implications of the deteriorating geopolitical situation in the region.

cards.headline: Russian Missile Strike on Kyiv Kills at Least 13 as Ukrainian Air Defenses Fall Short
cards.body:
A Russian missile barrage struck Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight, killing at least 13 people and wounding 33 others, according to Ukrainian authorities. The attack hit residential buildings, warehouses, a medical facility and an educational institution across multiple districts of the capital.

Among the targets was a children's hospital in the Solomianskyi district west of central Kyiv. The strike blew out windows and burned vehicles parked nearby. At least two residential buildings in the area were also reported hit. Explosions were heard from the city center around midnight Wednesday, earlier than typical Russian strike timing, with additional waves of attacks continuing into Thursday morning.

Ukraine's air force said Russia launched dozens of ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles along with 168 drones during the overnight bombardment. The weapons included Kinzhal and Zircon hypersonic missiles, Iskander and North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles, and Shahed drones.

In the broader Kyiv region, an attack on the Brovary district killed one man and wounded another. Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said an industrial facility was damaged and emergency services worked to extinguish fires at the site.

The strikes exposed Ukraine's vulnerability to continued Russian air attacks. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the assault demonstrated why stronger international support is needed. "While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world," Zelenskyy stated on social media. "And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously."

The attack prompted responses from neighboring NATO countries. Poland's military mobilized aircraft and activated air defenses in areas bordering Ukraine. Romania's defense ministry reported radar detection of aerial targets near the border overnight and scrambled two Spanish fighter jets and a Romanian helicopter. A drone entered Romanian airspace near Galati before crashing in an unpopulated area in Tulcea county.

Russia reported a large Ukrainian drone attack in return. Moscow's mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 250 drones flew toward the Moscow region between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, with most destroyed at considerable distance from the capital itself.

The latest strikes come as Ukraine escalates its own retaliatory attacks on Russian targets, including facilities supplying Moscow's military infrastructure. The attack on Kyiv also coincided with domestic political turmoil, as Zelenskyy dismissed senior aide Iryna Mudra following reports of searches related to alleged money laundering, extending a corruption scandal involving high-ranking officials.

cards.headline: North Korea fires suspected missile toward sea
cards.teaser: North Korea launched a suspected missile on Thursday, according to Japanese officials.
cards.body:
North Korea launched approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters on Thursday, according to South Korea's military. The launches occurred from the capital region around 5 p.m. local time.

The test came one day after North Korea rejected a U.S. decision to reduce the scope of joint military exercises with South Korea. The United States had scaled back the drills in an apparent attempt to restart diplomatic talks with North Korea.

cards.headline: Israel Opens Bidding for West Bank Settlement Project
cards.teaser: The UK foreign secretary condemned the move as an unacceptable and destructive act.
cards.body:
Israel opened bidding for a new settlement construction project in the West Bank, prompting swift international condemnation. Britain's foreign secretary criticized the decision as "an unacceptable and destructive act," reflecting broader concerns about Israeli settlement expansion in occupied territories.

The project's location in a sensitive area raises questions about its potential impact on future peace negotiations and regional stability.

cards.headline: Treasury deploys bond buyback program as borrowing costs hit 18-year high
cards.teaser: The Trump administration launched emergency measures to address rising long-term borrowing costs after the U.S.
cards.body:
Government borrowing costs across the U.S., UK, Germany, France, and Japan surged to multi-decade highs on Tuesday as geopolitical tensions escalated. The spike followed the collapse of US-Iran ceasefire negotiations on Monday night, with no progress made on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Rising concerns about inflation drove bond yields sharply higher across advanced economies.

In response to the market turmoil, the Trump administration launched a bond buyback program allowing the Treasury to repurchase its own debt in the secondary market. The initiative aims to temporarily reduce yields and stabilize markets. Critics argue the approach addresses symptoms rather than underlying fiscal problems, while policymakers face pressure to manage the bond market stress without triggering broader economic disruption.

cards.headline: China Sentences Evergrande Founder to Life in Prison
cards.teaser: Hui Ka Yan received a life sentence following the collapse of his property empire that triggered an extended crisis in the Chinese economy.
cards.body:
A Chinese court sentenced Hui Ka Yan, founder of the property developer Evergrande, to life in prison. The verdict marks a major turning point in the company's dramatic collapse, which left it burdened with more than $300 billion in liabilities.

Evergrande's downfall triggered a prolonged crisis across China's economy and financial system. The property sector, once a key engine of Chinese economic growth, was severely shaken by the developer's implosion and its cascading failures.

cards.headline: North Korea Dismisses Reduced US-South Korea Military Drills
cards.teaser: Kim Jong-un's sister said she was unaware of any communication with Washington, contradicting President Trump's claim that North Korea had responded to his outreach.
cards.body:
Kim Yo-jong, a senior adviser and sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, dismissed the significance of scaled-back military exercises between the United States and South Korea. She stated she was unaware of any communication between Pyongyang and Washington, contradicting President Trump's claims that Kim Jong-un had responded to his diplomatic outreach.

The denial came one day after North Korea launched approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters. Trump had announced the reduction in joint drills as an apparent overture to resume diplomacy, and claimed he was planning to meet Kim Jong-un later this year.

cards.headline: Israel Opens Bidding for West Bank Settlement Project
cards.teaser: The UK foreign secretary condemned the move as an unacceptable and destructive act.
cards.body:
Israel opened bidding for a new settlement construction project in the West Bank, prompting swift international condemnation. Britain's foreign secretary criticized the decision as "an unacceptable and destructive act," reflecting broader concerns about Israeli settlement expansion in occupied territories.

The project's location in a sensitive area raises questions about its potential impact on future peace negotiations and regional stability.

cards.headline: Former Liberian Vice President Charged in Drug Trafficking Investigation
cards.teaser: Jewel Howard-Taylor was arrested at Liberia's international airport and has not commented on the allegations.
cards.body:
Liberian authorities arrested former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor at the country's international airport as part of a drug-trafficking investigation. The arrest marks a significant moment in Liberian politics, with law enforcement targeting a former holder of one of the nation's highest constitutional offices.

Howard-Taylor has not made any public statements regarding the allegations since her detention.

cards.headline: Former Zambian Minister Killed in Security Raid on Opposition
cards.teaser: Police confirmed Mutotwe Kafwaya's death after growing demands for information about his whereabouts.
cards.body:
Zambian police confirmed that former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya died during a security raid targeting opposition members. The confirmation came after mounting public pressure and demands for information about his whereabouts.

Kafwaya's death during the operation has raised questions about the conduct of security forces and the treatment of opposition figures. The incident occurred as part of a broader security action against opposition members in Zambia.

cards.headline: Ecuador Intelligence Chief and Five Americans Die in Kenya Helicopter Crash
cards.teaser: Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife Stephany Hollihan were among seven people killed in the crash.
cards.body:
Seven people died when a safari helicopter crashed in northern Kenya on Wednesday morning. The victims included five American citizens, Ecuador's national intelligence director Michele Sensi-Contugi, and a Telemundo executive. Sensi-Contugi's wife was also among those killed in the accident.

Local police and the U.S. State Department confirmed all seven people onboard were killed in the remote area crash.

hero.headline: Pilot killed, two state police troopers injured in midair collision at Pennsylvania airport
hero.body:
A small plane and a Pennsylvania State Police helicopter collided at Carlisle Regional Airport on Thursday, killing the pilot of the plane and injuring two state troopers aboard the helicopter. The crash involved a midair collision between the two aircraft, according to officials.

The two Pennsylvania State Police troopers who were piloting the helicopter survived the impact and were taken for medical treatment. Both sustained injuries in what officials described as a very violent crash. The pilot of the small plane died in the collision.

The Federal Aviation Administration has opened an investigation into the crash. The collision occurred at the regional airport in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, though officials have not disclosed the specific circumstances that led to the two aircraft occupying the same airspace at the time of impact.

Pennsylvania State Police are cooperating fully with the FAA investigation. The type of small plane involved in the collision and the specific mission or flight path of the state police helicopter have not been made public by authorities.

Carlisle Regional Airport serves both civilian and law enforcement aircraft in the central Pennsylvania region. The airport is located in a busy airspace that accommodates various types of aviation operations.

The crash represents a rare event involving law enforcement aircraft. Despite the violent nature of the collision, both state troopers aboard the helicopter survived the impact, suggesting the aircraft maintained some degree of control before landing. The full sequence of events leading up to and following the collision will be determined through the ongoing investigation.

The survival of the helicopter crew despite the severity of the crash highlights the dangers that law enforcement pilots face during their operations. Midair collisions, while uncommon, are among the most serious aviation incidents that can occur.

Authorities have not yet announced the operational status of Carlisle Regional Airport following the collision. It remains unclear whether the airport has implemented any temporary closures or operational changes while the investigation proceeds.

The FAA typically conducts thorough investigations into midair collisions to determine contributing factors and identify any potential safety improvements. These investigations examine weather conditions, communication between aircraft, visibility, airport procedures, and pilot actions leading up to the collision.

The identities of the state police troopers injured in the crash and the pilot of the small plane have not been released by authorities. Officials have indicated that further details will be made available as the investigation progresses.

The incident will likely prompt a review of safety protocols at the airport and may lead to recommendations for preventing similar collisions in the future.

cards.headline: Trump administration changes policy on protected wild horses, sending them to slaughter
cards.teaser: The Trump administration has altered protections for wild horses, allowing them to be sent to slaughter facilities.
cards.body:
Wild horses that were previously protected under federal policy are now being sent to slaughter under changes implemented by the Trump administration. The New York Times reported on the policy shift affecting these animals.

The horses had been protected from slaughter, but the administration has reversed that protection. The change marks a significant shift in how the federal government manages wild horse populations on public lands.

cards.headline: Prince Harry and Meghan to return to United Kingdom this month
cards.teaser: Prince Harry and Meghan will move back to the United Kingdom later this month with their two children.
cards.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan are returning to the United Kingdom for an extended stay beginning this fall. Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, are enrolled to start at a school in September.

The move marks a return to Britain after the couple stepped back from their roles as working members of the royal family and relocated to the United States.

cards.headline: North Korea fires suspected missile toward sea
cards.teaser: North Korea launched a suspected missile on Thursday, according to Japanese officials.
cards.body:
North Korea launched approximately 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters on Thursday, according to South Korea's military. The launches occurred from the capital region around 5 p.m. local time.

The test came one day after North Korea rejected a U.S. decision to reduce the scope of joint military exercises with South Korea. The United States had scaled back the drills in an apparent attempt to restart diplomatic talks with North Korea.

cards.headline: At least 13 killed in air attack on Kyiv as Ukraine faces air defense shortages
cards.teaser: Ukrainian officials reported at least 13 deaths following what they called a massive attack on the capital on Thursday.
cards.body:
At least 13 people were killed and 33 injured in a heavy Russian missile attack on Kyiv overnight, according to the city's mayor Vitali Klitschko. The bombardment struck residential areas, warehouses, a medical facility and an educational institution across the capital and surrounding region.

Ukraine continues to struggle with insufficient air defense systems, limiting its ability to protect civilians from incoming missile strikes. The attack underscores the vulnerability of populated areas as Russia maintains its aerial assault campaign against the country.

cards.headline: Family of four including 14-year-old student dies in sea off Shoreham
cards.teaser: A London school paid tribute to a 14-year-old student and her family who died in the sea near Shoreham.
cards.body:
Ellen Wilkinson School for Girls in Ealing has paid tribute to Sara El-Khawas, 14, following her death in the sea off Shoreham. The school expressed its deep sadness at the loss of the student and her family members.

The family of four died in the water near the coastal town in West Sussex. The school community mourned the loss of Sara and her relatives.

cards.headline: Travelodge boss resigns following criticism over hotel safety and security
cards.teaser: The chief executive of Travelodge stepped down after facing criticism over the hotel chain's handling of safety issues.
cards.body:
Jo Boydell resigned as boss of Travelodge as the hotel chain works to address security concerns following a sexual assault at one of its properties. Boydell had faced criticism for how the company handled safety and security issues.

The resignation comes as the budget hotel chain tackles problems with safety protocols at its locations. Boydell's departure follows scrutiny of the company's response to security incidents affecting guests.

hero.headline: Treasury Department Expands Bond Buyback Program as Markets Remain Volatile
hero.body:
The U.S. Treasury announced it is doubling its buyback of government debt in an effort to stabilize bond markets as yield rates hit 20-year highs. The 30-year treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007 this week, alongside similar spikes in 10-year and 20-year treasury notes.

The rapid increase in yields prompted immediate concern about borrowing costs for consumers. Since mortgages and other major loans are backed by treasury securities, higher yields translate directly into higher interest rates for borrowers. Following the Treasury's announcement on Wednesday, yields declined as the department signaled its intention to "provide greater liquidity support" to the long-term bond market.

The intervention comes as officials at the Federal Reserve remain divided over how to address persistent inflation. Minutes from the Fed's July meeting, released Wednesday, revealed ongoing disagreement among board members about the appropriate policy path. While a majority of voting members agreed to keep interest rates unchanged at their current range of 3.5% to 3.75%, three members indicated they would prefer higher rates. According to the minutes, "many participants assessed that policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation did not decline."

Inflation has proved stubborn despite geopolitical disruptions. The annualized U.S. inflation rate stood at 3.4% in July, down from a three-year peak of 4.2% in May but still notably above 2025 levels. Oil prices have been a significant contributor to price pressures, with AAA reporting that August gas prices were on track to reach record highs at $4.08 per gallon, roughly one dollar more than the previous year.

The Treasury's expanded buyback program follows earlier Trump administration interventions to support financial markets. The administration recently partnered with the Japanese government, which holds substantial U.S. treasury securities, to intervene in currency markets. Investors have expressed heightened anxiety following the expiration of a two-month ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran on Monday, with no peace talks currently scheduled.

Stock markets responded positively to the Treasury's announcement, with the Nasdaq futures ticking up modestly Wednesday. The S&P 500 closed at another record high last week, though broader market volatility persists. The stock market has remained resilient despite inflationary pressures, buoyed by strong investment in artificial intelligence.

The Federal Reserve faces pressure from multiple directions. Rising inflation creates pressure to increase interest rates toward the Fed's 2% target, yet the White House has been pressing the central bank to lower rates instead. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who took office in May, has remained largely silent about his position on the appropriate policy direction, though he has appeared skeptical of additional Fed intervention.

cards.headline: Evergrande Founder Hui Ka Yan Sentenced to Life in Prison
cards.teaser: A Chinese court sentenced the founder of collapsed property developer Evergrande to life in prison.
cards.body:
Hui Ka Yan, founder of Chinese property developer Evergrande, has been sentenced to life in prison by a Chinese court. The sentencing marks a significant moment in the aftermath of Evergrande's collapse, which left the company with more than $300 billion in liabilities.

Evergrande's failure sent shockwaves through China's property sector and broader financial system, triggering a prolonged crisis in the Chinese economy. The life sentence represents one of the harshest penalties handed down to a major Chinese business figure in recent years.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise Following New Threats Against Iran
cards.teaser: Oil prices jumped after President Trump issued new threats against Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices surged after the expiration of a two-month ceasefire between the US and Iran on Monday, with no diplomatic resolution achieved. Brent crude rose above $90 a barrel for the first time since late July. The escalation reflects renewed tensions following Trump's demand that Iran "surrender," while Iranian officials signaled they would adopt a more aggressive stance if negotiations with the US fail.

The price movement underscores trader concerns about potential disruptions to Middle Eastern energy supplies. Bond markets also experienced volatility as investors assessed the implications of the deteriorating geopolitical situation in the region.

cards.headline: Moderna Stock Surges 177% on Shift to Cancer Treatments
cards.teaser: Moderna's stock climbed 177% as the company pivoted its focus to cancer therapies.
cards.body:
Moderna's shares surged as the company repositioned itself from a Covid-19 vaccine maker to a cancer treatment developer. The biotech firm saw its fortunes decline sharply as demand for coronavirus vaccines plummeted from pandemic-era peaks.

While public attention focused on falling vaccine sales, Moderna had been developing cancer therapies using its messenger RNA technology platform. The same technology that enabled rapid Covid vaccine development is now being applied to oncology treatments. Investors responded positively to early results and the company's strategic shift toward a larger and more stable market opportunity.

cards.headline: Middle East Conflict Redirects Air Travel Through Asian Hubs
cards.teaser: Airlines are routing long-haul flights through Seoul and other Asian cities instead of Dubai and Middle Eastern airports.
cards.body:
The war involving Iran has sharply reduced transit traffic at Middle Eastern airports, creating new opportunities for aviation hubs in Asia and other regions. Airlines are rerouting passengers through cities like Seoul as conflicts make traditional Middle Eastern transfer points less viable.

The shift represents a potentially significant change in global air travel patterns, at least temporarily. Middle Eastern airports including Dubai had invested heavily in becoming major international transit hubs over the past two decades. Asian airports are now capturing that connecting traffic as airlines avoid airspace and facilities in the conflict zone.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Announces Additional Economic Measures Against Iran
cards.teaser: President Trump pledged tougher economic measures targeting Iran and countries that support it.
cards.body:
Following the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire on Monday with no diplomatic resolution, the Trump administration vowed to implement stronger economic measures against Iran and countries providing support to it. Trump demanded that Tehran "put up the white flag of surrender" in a Fox News interview.

The escalating tensions triggered immediate market reactions, with Brent crude oil rising above $90 a barrel for the first time since late July. Iran signaled it would adopt a more aggressive stance if negotiations with the US failed, while bond markets remained volatile as investors assessed the geopolitical uncertainty.

cards.headline: Travelodge Chief Executive Resigns Amid Safety Concerns
cards.teaser: Travelodge's boss stepped down as the hotel chain addresses security issues following a sexual assault at one of its properties.
cards.body:
Jo Boydell resigned as chief executive of Travelodge as the hotel chain works to address safety and security problems. Boydell faced criticism for the company's handling of issues related to guest safety and security protocols.

The resignation followed a sexual assault incident at a Travelodge hotel that raised questions about the chain's security measures. The company has been under pressure to strengthen safety procedures and oversight at its properties across its hotel network.

hero.headline: LG Display unveils FLiPP OLED technology with improved brightness and lifespan
hero.body:
LG Display announced a new OLED screen technology called FLiPP that increases brightness by up to 1.6 times compared to existing OLED displays while extending their lifespan. The technology addresses one of the longstanding limitations of OLED screens, which have historically struggled with brightness levels and degradation over time.

The FLiPP technology represents a significant advancement in display manufacturing. OLED screens are known for their superior contrast and color reproduction compared to traditional LCD panels, but lower peak brightness and concerns about burn-in have limited their adoption in certain applications. By improving both brightness and longevity, the new technology could expand the use of OLED displays across more device categories.

LG Display indicated the technology could be used in screens up to 100 inches in size, suggesting applications beyond smartphones and tablets. The company has been a leading supplier of OLED panels for televisions, computer monitors, and mobile devices. Competitors are also advancing display technology, with Samsung showcasing a 300Hz OLED display designed for gaming laptops at the same time.

The timing of the announcement coincides with growing demand for high-quality displays across consumer electronics. Brighter screens improve visibility in outdoor settings and well-lit rooms, while longer lifespans reduce the total cost of ownership for consumers and manufacturers. The technology could influence product development cycles for companies that rely on LG Display as a supplier.

LG Display has not provided a timeline for when FLiPP-based screens will appear in commercial products or disclosed which manufacturers have committed to using the technology. The company also has not specified the exact mechanisms behind the brightness and lifespan improvements or whether the technology requires changes to manufacturing processes.

cards.headline: Binance launches Agent OS to enable AI-powered cryptocurrency trading
cards.teaser: Binance introduced software that allows artificial intelligence agents to execute trades on its platform, with users responsible for oversight.
cards.body:
Binance released Agent OS, a new system that enables AI agents to conduct cryptocurrency trading on its exchange. The platform works with tools including ChatGPT, Claude Code, and Cursor, allowing automated trading decisions based on AI analysis.

The company placed responsibility for monitoring and controlling the AI agents on users themselves. This approach shifts oversight duties to individual traders rather than implementing centralized controls, raising questions about risk management as automated trading systems become more accessible to retail investors.

cards.headline: Samsung schedules August 27 event for new Galaxy S26 model
cards.teaser: Samsung confirmed it will hold an event later this month to reveal another device in its Galaxy S26 lineup.
cards.body:
Samsung has confirmed an event scheduled for August 27 to introduce a new addition to its Galaxy S26 lineup. The company sent official invitations for the announcement, though Samsung has not specified which model variant will be unveiled.

Industry reports suggest the event may feature the Galaxy S26 FE, a more budget-friendly option within the S26 family. Design details and specifications have emerged online ahead of the official reveal, including information about hardware configuration.

cards.headline: Waymo opens next-generation robotaxi to all riders in three cities
cards.teaser: Waymo expanded access to its newer, more affordable autonomous vehicle called the Waymo Ojai across three metropolitan areas.
cards.body:
Waymo has launched its next-generation robotaxi, the Waymo Ojai, to all riders in three cities. The vehicle is designed to be cheaper to operate than previous models, supporting the company's strategy to achieve mass scale in the autonomous vehicle market.

The Ojai represents a key milestone in Waymo's path toward profitability. By reducing per-vehicle costs, the company can serve more customers while strengthening its competitive position in the self-driving taxi industry.

cards.headline: NASA cancels rescue mission for Swift gamma-ray observatory
cards.teaser: NASA decided against launching a mission to save the Swift Observatory, which is expected to fall back to Earth later this year.
cards.body:
NASA called off plans to rescue the Swift gamma-ray observatory, a space telescope that has been studying cosmic gamma-ray bursts and other high-energy phenomena. Without intervention, the spacecraft is projected to reenter the atmosphere before the end of 2026.

The Swift Observatory has operated in space for over two decades, providing data on some of the most energetic events in the universe. The decision not to pursue a rescue mission likely reflects cost considerations and the spacecraft's age, though NASA has not detailed its reasoning.

cards.headline: OpenAI introduces new privacy protections for enterprise customers
cards.teaser: OpenAI announced enhanced privacy measures for business clients using its AI services.
cards.body:
OpenAI has introduced new privacy protections for enterprise customers, reflecting growing competition with Anthropic over data security capabilities. Both companies are vying to offer stronger safeguards as corporate clients increasingly prioritize how their sensitive information is handled on AI platforms.

Enterprise customers handling confidential data have made privacy a critical factor in choosing between AI providers. These protections serve as a key differentiator in the market as companies evaluate which platform best secures their business information.

cards.headline: Amazon targets 500 US neighborhoods for drone delivery by year end
cards.teaser: Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air drone delivery service to 500 neighborhoods across the United States by the end of 2026.
cards.body:
Amazon plans to expand its Prime Air drone delivery service to nearly 500 U.S. cities by the end of 2026, significantly broadening access to automated aerial package delivery across the country.

The expansion of drone delivery presents both benefits and challenges for residents. Faster delivery times offer convenience, but the growth of these services raises concerns about noise, privacy, and airspace congestion as the technology reaches more populated areas.

hero.headline: Verstappen extends Red Bull contract through 2030
hero.body:
Four-time Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed a new contract extension with Red Bull that will keep him with the team through the end of the 2030 season, ending months of speculation about his future in the sport.

The Dutch driver had been linked with potential moves to Mercedes and McLaren and had previously suggested he might retire from Formula One altogether due to his dissatisfaction with the new regulations introduced this season. However, ahead of his home race at the Dutch Grand Prix, the 28-year-old confirmed he would continue his partnership with Red Bull through the remainder of the decade.

Verstappen's previous contract was set to expire at the end of 2028 but included performance-based break clauses that would have allowed him to leave if he chose to do so. The new deal extends his commitment by two additional years.

"The team is like a second family for me and I feel very at home," Verstappen said in a statement. "I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely and we have shared many incredible moments and won four world championships."

The timing of the announcement is particularly significant given Red Bull's current struggles. The team has faced challenges adapting to the new technical regulations this season, while Mercedes has emerged with a dominant car. Verstappen currently sits sixth in the world championship standings, 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with only two second-place finishes to his name so far this year.

Verstappen has been vocal about his dislike for the new regulations and their emphasis on energy management, sentiments shared by many other drivers on the grid. Despite these frustrations, he expressed confidence in Red Bull's ability to recover and return to championship contention.

The driver also highlighted his positive working relationship with Laurent Mekies, Red Bull's team principal who took over from Christian Horner last July. "Getting to work with Laurent now for over a year has also been great," Verstappen said. "I see a clear vision he has for the team. Everyone in Milton Keynes believes in what we are building and I am looking forward to the next chapter, fighting for more victories and competing for championships."

Mekies emphasized the importance of securing Verstappen's future with the team. "Very few partnerships in sport achieve what Max and this team have," the team principal said. "Since the very beginning, Max has embodied everything that makes Oracle Red Bull Racing special: uncompromising competitiveness, relentless determination and the courage to challenge convention."

Verstappen will be 33 years old when his contract expires in 2030, potentially allowing him to pursue additional years in Formula One beyond that point should he wish to continue racing.

cards.headline: Inter Milan agree deal to sign Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones
cards.teaser: Curtis Jones is set to join Inter Milan after the Italian club agreed a transfer worth 35 million euros with Liverpool.
cards.body:
Inter Milan has agreed to sign Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones for 35 million euros, equivalent to £30 million. The deal will bring the English midfielder to Serie A following his departure from the club where he developed through the academy system.

Jones, who progressed through Liverpool's youth ranks to establish himself in the first team, will now begin a new chapter in Italian football as Inter strengthens their midfield ahead of the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Tottenham in talks to sign Manchester City attackers Savinho and Marmoush
cards.teaser: Tottenham has opened negotiations with Manchester City to sign forwards Omar Marmoush and Savinho in a potential double deal.
cards.body:
Tottenham has opened negotiations with Manchester City to sign attacking players Omar Marmoush and Savinho. The potential transfers are part of a broader clearout at the Etihad Stadium as City reshapes their squad during the transfer window.

The dual signing would strengthen Tottenham's attacking options for the upcoming season, with both players currently part of Manchester City's roster.

cards.headline: Sabalenka loses to Bejlek at Cincinnati Open ahead of US Open defense
cards.teaser: Aryna Sabalenka suffered a surprising defeat to Sara Bejlek at the Cincinnati Open, continuing a difficult stretch before the US Open.
cards.body:
Aryna Sabalenka lost to Sara Bejlek at the Cincinnati Open in an unexpected result that extends the top player's recent struggles. Sabalenka is the defending US Open champion and had been using the Cincinnati tournament to prepare for her title defense.

The loss represents another setback in what has been a difficult period for Sabalenka. The Cincinnati Open serves as one of the final tune-up events before the US Open begins, making the timing of the defeat particularly concerning for the reigning champion as she looks to defend her title.

cards.headline: Francesca Hennessy in talks for undisputed bantamweight title fight
cards.teaser: British boxer Francesca Hennessy is negotiating a fight with undisputed bantamweight world champion Dina Thorslund in the United Kingdom.
cards.body:
Francesca Hennessy is in talks to face undisputed bantamweight world champion Dina Thorslund later this year. The fight would take place in the United Kingdom.

This potential matchup would give the British boxer an opportunity to challenge for all the major titles in the bantamweight division.

cards.headline: England all-rounder Sam Curran ruled out for summer with groin injury
cards.teaser: Sam Curran will miss the rest of the English cricket summer after requiring surgery for a groin injury.
cards.body:
England all-rounder Sam Curran has been ruled out for the remainder of the summer cricket season due to a groin injury requiring surgery. The injury ends any possibility of Curran making a return to the Test team during this season.

Curran had been hoping to work his way back into England's Test squad during the summer. The injury and subsequent surgery mean he will not be available for selection as England continues its Test schedule in the coming months.

cards.headline: BBC Sport pundits predict Premier League top four for 2026-27 season
cards.teaser: Twenty-six BBC Sport football experts have shared their predictions for who will win the Premier League title and finish in the top four positions.
cards.body:
BBC Sport asked 26 football pundits to predict the 2026-27 Premier League season, including their picks for the title winner and the four clubs most likely to finish in the top positions.

The predictions offer expert insight into how the upcoming campaign may unfold as Premier League teams prepare for the new season.

hero.headline: Prince Harry and Meghan to Move Back to United Kingdom
hero.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle plan to relocate from the United States to the United Kingdom with their children Archie and Lilibet, according to multiple reports. The move, set to take place this month, marks a significant shift for the couple who stepped back from royal duties in 2020 and subsequently settled in California.

The decision has prompted widespread speculation in Britain about what prompted the couple's return. Since leaving their roles as senior working members of the royal family, Harry and Meghan have built independent careers in the entertainment and media industries while residing in Montecito, California. Their departure from royal life included a widely publicized interview and documentary series detailing their experiences within the royal family.

The couple's children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, were born in the United States and have spent most of their lives there. The relocation will represent their first sustained period living in the United Kingdom. Harry has maintained some ties to Britain through periodic visits for family events and legal proceedings related to media privacy cases.

The timing and logistics of the move have attracted considerable attention from both British and American media outlets. The couple has maintained a complicated relationship with the British press since their departure, citing media intrusion as one factor in their decision to leave. Their return raises questions about how they will navigate public life and their relationship with the royal family going forward.

Neither representatives for Harry and Meghan nor Buckingham Palace have issued official statements about the reported move. The couple's previous residence in the United Kingdom was Frogmore Cottage on the Windsor estate, though reports indicate they vacated that property. The nature of their living arrangements upon return and whether they will resume any official duties remains unconfirmed.

cards.headline: Sons of Anarchy Cast Reunites for FX Limited Series
cards.teaser: Charlie Hunnam and original cast members will return for a new FX series titled Legends.
cards.body:
FX has ordered a limited series called Legends featuring Charlie Hunnam and members of the original Sons of Anarchy cast. Kurt Sutter, creator of the original series, has publicly reacted to the announcement of the new show.

The series represents a reunion of the cast from Sons of Anarchy, which concluded its original run years ago. Details about the specific format and storyline of Legends have been described as involving a wild twist, though the exact nature of the series has not been fully detailed.

cards.headline: Goalhanger Hires Tom Miceli to Lead TV and Film Expansion
cards.teaser: The British podcasting company behind The Rest is Football is accelerating its screen content development.
cards.body:
Goalhanger, the British podcasting company, has hired Tom Miceli as head of IP development to expand its television and film operations. Miceli joins from WME in the newly created role focused on developing screen content from the company's podcast properties.

The company produces The Rest is Football, which recently launched as a Netflix show covering the World Cup. The hire signals Goalhanger's intention to grow its presence in television and film beyond its podcast origins.

cards.headline: Michal R. Roskam's Le Faux Soir Set as San Sebastián Closing Film
cards.teaser: The Belgian-French World War II resistance drama will close the San Sebastián Film Festival after premiering in Toronto.
cards.body:
Belgian-French director Michaël R. Roskam's World War II resistance drama Le Faux Soir will close this year's San Sebastián Film Festival. The film screens in the Official Selection out of competition.

Roskam, known for his earlier film Bullhead, will premiere Le Faux Soir at Toronto International Film Festival before its European debut at San Sebastián.

cards.headline: Channel 4 ADHD Documentary Draws Charity Complaint
cards.teaser: An ADHD charity has complained about a Channel 4 documentary titled The Great ADHD Myth?
cards.body:
A charity focused on ADHD has filed a complaint regarding a Channel 4 documentary. One newspaper has described The Great ADHD Myth? as the most controversial show of the year.

The documentary's title and content have prompted criticism from advocacy organizations working in the ADHD space. The show has generated significant media attention and public debate since its broadcast.

cards.headline: China's Pingyao Film Festival Announces 10th Edition Dates
cards.teaser: The festival founded by director Jia Zhangke will run from September 24 to 30 in Shanxi Province.
cards.body:
The Pingyao International Film Festival will hold its 10th edition from September 24 to 30 at the Pingyao Festival Palace in Shanxi Province. The festival was founded in 2017 by director Jia Zhangke.

The festival's programming includes four main areas: Screening, Market, Cultivation and Academics. The Screening section features Crouching Tigers, a program for emerging directors, alongside selections of international and domestic films.

cards.headline: Epic Studios Partners with Rusk Media on 50 Vertical Drama Series
cards.teaser: The Indian production deal aims to create the country's largest library of vertical drama intellectual property.
cards.body:
Epic Studios in India has partnered with Rusk Media Private Limited to produce 50 original vertical drama series. The collaboration seeks to establish India's largest library of owned vertical drama intellectual property.

The series will cover mythology, drama, mystery, thriller and romance genres. All productions will debut on Alright! TV, Rusk Media's platform for vertical drama content designed for mobile viewing.

hero.headline: Democrats lead Republicans by 8 points in new congressional poll
hero.teaser: A new survey shows Democrats ahead of Republicans on a generic ballot as midterm elections approach.
hero.body:
Democrats hold an 8-point advantage over Republicans on a generic congressional ballot, according to a poll from Emerson College and The Hill. The survey found 50.7 percent of respondents would back a Democrat if midterm elections were held immediately, compared to 43 percent who would support a Republican. Another 6.3 percent remained undecided.

The polling results provide a snapshot of voter sentiment as both parties prepare for the midterm elections. Generic ballot surveys ask voters which party they would support without naming specific candidates, offering a broad measure of the political environment.

cards.headline: Treasury deploys bond buyback program as borrowing costs hit 18-year high
cards.teaser: The Trump administration launched emergency measures to address rising long-term borrowing costs after the U.S.
cards.body:
Government borrowing costs across the U.S., UK, Germany, France, and Japan surged to multi-decade highs on Tuesday as geopolitical tensions escalated. The spike followed the collapse of US-Iran ceasefire negotiations on Monday night, with no progress made on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Rising concerns about inflation drove bond yields sharply higher across advanced economies.

In response to the market turmoil, the Trump administration launched a bond buyback program allowing the Treasury to repurchase its own debt in the secondary market. The initiative aims to temporarily reduce yields and stabilize markets. Critics argue the approach addresses symptoms rather than underlying fiscal problems, while policymakers face pressure to manage the bond market stress without triggering broader economic disruption.

cards.headline: Army reverses course on new ROTC academic standards after internal dispute
cards.teaser: The Army withdrew proposed minimum academic standards for college students in ROTC programs days after issuing them.
cards.body:
The Army pulled back new minimum academic standards for Reserve Officers Training Corps college students earlier this month, just days after announcing them. The reversal followed internal disagreement and concerns that senior leaders were not adequately consulted before the standards were issued.

The episode highlights tensions within the Army over how to balance recruitment needs with maintaining quality standards for future officers. ROTC programs train college students to become commissioned officers upon graduation, making academic requirements a significant factor in shaping the officer corps.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance raises $5 million at fundraiser in the Hamptons
cards.teaser: The vice president hosted young Republican donors at a fundraiser that drew donors in their 20s and 30s.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance hosted a fundraiser in Southampton, New York that brought in more than $5 million from roughly 35 attendees. The event, held at the home of 1789 Capital President Omeed Malik, targeted younger Republican donors in their 20s and 30s.

The gathering included Donald Trump Jr., Polymarket founder Shayne Coplan, and other prominent figures in Republican finance networks. The fundraiser reflects Vance's efforts to build donor relationships as he prepares for a potential 2028 presidential campaign.

cards.headline: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin pauses enforcement actions after congressional appeals
cards.teaser: The former congressman has built a reputation for responding to requests from his previous colleagues on Capitol Hill.
cards.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has drawn attention for granting favors to former congressional colleagues, including pausing ICE traffic stops and delaying border security construction along the Texas border. The decisions came after personal appeals from friends in Congress, according to reports.

Mullin served 13 years in Washington as a House member and senator before joining the Cabinet. His willingness to accommodate congressional requests has occasionally put him at odds with White House priorities and other administration officials.

cards.headline: Rubio edges Vance in hypothetical 2028 presidential matchups
cards.teaser: The Secretary of State performed slightly better than the vice president in polling against potential Democratic candidates.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio outperformed Vice President Vance in four of five hypothetical 2028 presidential matchups against Democratic candidates, according to an Emerson College and The Hill poll. The one exception was a matchup against former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, where both performed similarly.

The survey offers an early look at how potential Republican candidates might fare in the next presidential election. Both Rubio and Vance are considered likely contenders for the Republican nomination in 2028.

cards.headline: Data center opposition reshapes midterm campaigns across party lines
cards.teaser: Candidates are distancing themselves from AI data center projects as grassroots resistance builds momentum.
cards.body:
A growing movement against AI data centers is forcing midterm candidates in both parties to retreat from projects their leaders previously supported. What began as local opposition to individual facilities has evolved into a broader populist movement with cross-partisan appeal.

The shift represents a break from the bipartisan consensus that enabled the expansion of data centers across the country. Candidates are responding to grassroots pressure by distancing themselves from data center developments, even in cases where party leaders championed the economic benefits of such projects.
